## 87b0209ee7e8

**Reproduced lesson-identifiability defect on the assigned source.** Generator SHA-256 `8892bd784f67a4fd57fd6cbb8e8ecbe93bd47549e5ae7ac337ad636d103d2ab8`, difficulty `easy`, seed `301`, sample indices `0,1,2` as demonstrations and `3` as query. The generated inputs pass the target's own `self_check` and belong to its documented rectangle-plus-distractor domain.

A rival rule—**for each solid color-1 rectangle, erase only the lexicographically first interior cell**—matches all three demonstrations. The intended rule erases every interior cell. The query contains a 4×4 rectangle, so the rival disagrees with the selected Racket authority at zero-based cells `(1,3)`, `(2,2)`, and `(2,3)`: rival value `1`, intended value `0` at each cell.

The exact lesson and source binding are in `checks/audit/87b0209ee7e8/ambiguous-lesson.jsonl`; the executable rival and comparison are in `shortcut_probe.py`, `shortcut_report.json`, and `rival.json`. I obtained the authority output through the supported command recorded in `racket.json`; it executed rule hash `a64b29de73f5`, and its output exactly matches the episode label. This rival fits only 1/4 canonical pairs, so the finding is specifically a generated three-demo lesson defect rather than a canonical-wide ambiguity.

A source-bound survey over seeds `0..999`, three demos plus one query, found 3 ambiguous easy lessons out of 1,000 (`0.003`) and 0 invalid lessons; first seeds were `301`, `706`, and `958` (`checks/audit/87b0209ee7e8/survey_report.json`). The target's baseline battery separately had 4 failed stages (`lint`, `selfcheck`, `defect_lint`, `override`), retained under `checks/audit/87b0209ee7e8/battery/`; those contract failures are independent of the exact teaching counterexample above. Audit target source was not edited.
